Name: Goodbye My Danish Farm
Author: heathinwillows
Description:
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/77112253-1770708929.png[/img]

In grandpas prime (his name is Jack) he found this small secluded place hidden in pelican town. He cultivated the land with such passion and love, he grew top notch quality crops, took care of his animals like a good father. Then the day comes that he fells inlove..

In Pelican Town in 1963, mayor [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Lewis]Lewis Del Mar[/url] and [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Twist]Jack Twist[/url] (grandpa) are hired by rancher [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Marnie]Marnie[/url] to herd her sheep through the summer on grazing pastures on Danish Farm. After a night of heavy drinking, Jack makes a pass at Lewis. While initially reluctant, Lewis becomes receptive, and he and Jack did the "woohoo" in their tent. Despite Lewis telling Jack that it was a one-time incident, they develop an intimate and emotional relationship. Near the end of their work contract, Lewis and Jack have a brawl that leaves both of them bloodied. Before parting ways, Lewis offhandedly laments that he left one of his shirts on the farm.

Lewis continued doing his duties as a mayor, although sometimes he wants to work a different job so he went to Marnie again and seek for work. Marnie, who happens to observed Jack and Lewis engaging in homosexual activity on the farm, tells him he has no work for guys who "stem the rose". Jack moves to ZuZu City for a bit, where he meets [url=https://h3h3.fandom.com/wiki/Trisha_Paytas]"random lady from jojamart"[/url] they marry and have a daughter/son/non binary child (you the farmer).

After four years apart, Jack visits Lewis. Upon meeting, they kiss passionately, which a stunned Marnie inadvertently sees. At a motel room, Jack wants them to create a life together, but Lewis refuses to abandon his job as a mayor and is haunted by a childhood memory of his father showing him the body of a man who was tortured and killed for suspected homosexuality.

Lewis and Jack meet infrequently for private "fishing trips" while their respective marriages and job deteriorate. One blooming awesome day Lewis had put divorce files in 1975. Upon hearing about it, Jack drives to Pelican Town and tells Lewis that they should live together, but Lewis refuses to quit his job as a mayor.

Lewis has a brief romantic relationship with Marnie, a rancher. Jack befriended [url=https://stardew-valley-expanded.fandom.com/wiki/Marlon]Marlon[/url], and it is implied that Jack and Marlon have a brief affair. At the end of a tryst disguised as a fishing trip, Lewis says he cannot see Jack again for months due to work demands. The pair argue, before Jack embraces a crying Lewis.

A postcard Lewis sent Jack is returned stamped with "Deceased". Lewis calls Jack's phone number. the random lady from jojamart answers and says Jack died when a car tire exploded in his face. While hearing what happened, Lewis envisions Jack listening to Mitski's song [url=https://youtu.be/ohxu-pA7o64?si=rD46PUIF7YNB455x]Goodbye My Danish Sweethear[/url]t. Random lady from jojamart says Jack requested his ashes be scattered on a small tree that he planted on Danish Farm as fertilizer.

Lewis visits Jack's parents hoping to carry out his wish. Jack's father declares that Jack's ashes will be interred in a family plot. Jack's mother allows Ennis to visit Jack's old bedroom. Lewis finds the shirt he thought he left on the mountain, which Jack had secretly kept, nested inside one of Jack's shirts. Lewis embraces the shirts and silently weeps. Jack's mother allows him to keep them.

Years later, an aging Lewis lives alone and reclusive in the Mayor's Manor still doing his job as a mayor. He heard the news of a new person coming to Pelican Town to tend on the now abandoned Danish Farm is actually Jack's child. Lewis hesitates to come and welcome the new farmer due to upcoming work commitments, then agrees to do it anyway. As he's about to leave his manor to ready the things for the new farmer, he forgets his jacket, he then looked for it in the closet where the two shirts hang, Jack's shirt now inside Lewis's. Next to them, tacked to the closet door, is a postcard of Danish Farm. With tears in his eyes, he stares at the mementos, and says, "Jack, I swear..."
